decision: Foundation only: pnpm workspace, core/app/adapter/suite packages, JCS reserved at @ix/jcs, no crypto and no signing
reason: Protocol behavior, signatures, and key handling wait for later tickets and a human security reviewer

decision: Negotiation phases are a pure state machine in @ix/a2a-ext-negotiation. Messages are typed data. Each message carries a signature placeholder that is not checked, and the session records verification as deferred. The round cap and the clock are inputs. No JCS, keys, mandate checks, or approval cryptography.
reason: The director asked for the phase rules before any signing design. A human security reviewer still has to accept that design before the placeholder can be replaced.

decision: A2A-Extensions activation is the exact intersection of requested and supported URIs for the four https://w3id.org/a2a-job/ext/*/v1 profiles. A requested URI that is not supported is ignored and is not replaced by another version. Negotiation activates only when mandate, approval, and transcript activate in the same request. The Agent Card declaration lists all four as required.
reason: The spec puts required extensions on the client and forbids answering with a different version.

decision: publish, query, and subscribe run in process on an injected store. The in-memory store lives in @ix/adapters. @ix/node does not import it. Closed mode refuses public publish. Expired events are discarded. Unknown kinds and tags are stored. id and sig are caller-supplied and unverified. There is no listening port. No new kind or tag is registered.
reason: Signatures and JCS remain stopped for the human security reviewer. PR #3 is the unmerged canonicalization work. The relay must not invent a hash or check a signature.

decision: Mock poster and worker agents in @ix/agents drive @ix/a2a-ext-negotiation through an injected relay board. Conformance items messages-match-types, proposals-stay-inside-mandate, and responds-within-deadline pass only for structure, a private numeric bound, and an injected clock. Items agent-card-declares-extensions, extensions-header-echo, and ignores-instructions-in-free-text stay pending. id, sig, prevHash, and transcriptHash stay caller-supplied placeholders. Kind x-mock/negotiation-message and tag x-job are private to the trial and are not profile vocabulary. @ix/a2a-ext-mandate stays a stub. Human approvals in the mock are scripted decisions.
reason: The director asked for a private trial of the phase machine. A pass is not a verified signature. A verifier who did not write the change still has to accept the three status flips. PR #3 remains the unmerged canonicalization work.

decision: deploy/local/compose.yaml runs the in-memory relay and the mock agents for a private trial. scripts/local-ix.mjs refuses every bind except 127.0.0.1. The compose file publishes no host ports. Poster and worker share the node network namespace so they can use that loopback. Drive does not start the listener.
reason: Public exposure is out of scope. The listener is not an A2A endpoint and it does not check signatures.

decision: Mock agreement linkage is the placeholder transcript-unverified-<amount>. It is not a hash. A draft whose amount differs from that placeholder, or from the offer already accepted, is not the same history. Agents re-check the amount against their private bound before applying a draft and before sending approval. Dates read by the mock are RFC 3339 calendar timestamps. Money is an integer number of JPY. A job post requires agentCard, description, budgetMin, budgetMax, and requiredSkills.
reason: An independent verifier showed a later draft could change the amount under one constant placeholder, and that date and job fields were looser than the spec. Signatures stay deferred.

decision: A job post's budget is two flat fields, budgetMin and budgetMax. Each is a money object. The spec example no longer nests them under budget.min and budget.max.
reason: The director asked the spec to match the implementation. Behavior is unchanged.

decision: Conformance item ignores-instructions-in-free-text passes only for the twelve cases in injectionCases, each executed against the mock agents and the relay. Free text does not change price, bounds, hours, scope, deadline, decision, round, or signature state. Contact details are redacted in the human-facing copy. @ix/verify checks message schema, phase-machine replay, bounds, and deadlines. checkSignature, checkJcs, checkJws, and checkPrevHash return deferred and do not hash.
reason: The director asked for the free-text suite without treating the signature placeholder as a check. A verifier who did not write the change still has to accept the item 6 status flip. PR #3 remains the unmerged canonicalization work.

decision: verify-ix-node drive starts the relay on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port, runs the mock poster and worker, writes evidence, and stops those processes. Doctor stays read-only. docs/feature-map.md lists what works and what is pending. The Nightly workflow runs pnpm check, pnpm conformance, and drive.
reason: The director asked the verification skill to launch the private trial. The listener still refuses every bind except 127.0.0.1 and publishes no port.

decision: Item 6 delivers deadline instructions through the relay: before the deadline the structured date stays, and after the deadline a stored note is read and does not draw a reply. Contact redaction also removes unhyphenated and international numbers, full-width and obfuscated emails, and bidi or zero-width hiding. Title, skills, deliverables, currency, and counterparty substitution are separate cases. Deliverable contacts are scrubbed out of the agreement.
reason: An independent verifier showed the first deadline case never reached the relay, and that contact scrubbing and several free-text fields were outside the twelve cases. Items 1 and 2 stay pending. Signatures stay deferred.

decision: Canonical bytes are RFC 8785 from @ix/jcs. The prevHash digest is SHA-256 of that UTF-8, lowercase hex, from hashCanonicalBody. It does not remove signature, parse JSON text, or Unicode-normalize. Non-JSON values are rejected. Nesting stops at 64 containers. No JWS and no keys.
reason: The spec requires one hash and does not name an encoding. Hex stands until a security reviewer replaces it. Duplicate keys are invisible on a JavaScript object, so this change does not reject them. Green CI is not acceptance.

decision: Wire JSON goes through parseJson before canonicalization. Duplicate keys and integers outside ±9007199254740991 are rejected from the text. Proxies are rejected. signingInputExcludingSignature is the JWS payload: JCS text with the top-level signature removed. hashCanonicalBody and hashExcludingSignature are digests, not that payload. Nesting cap 64 is ours, not RFC 8785. Array width is uncapped.
reason: Review of PR 3. In-memory JavaScript numbers, including RFC appendix B, still canonicalize. No JWS and no keys. Green CI is not acceptance.

decision: Term-by-term negotiation is a pure machine in @ix/a2a-ext-negotiation (openTermSession, applyTermMessage, buildTermAgreement) with the core sheet ix:core/1 and ix:sheet/web-site/1. A term is fixed only when the other side accepts an equal value. Reopen, add, and drop need the other side's accept. Rounds are counted per term. The agreement is the fixed terms sorted by termId and must be rebuilt identically from the history before the humans decide. ix:initial-spec is an optional core term of type documents: per-file SHA-256 and a manifest, no file bodies. @ix/agents runTermTrial drives scripted poster and worker mandates in process.
reason: The director chose typed terms fixed one at a time over free-text checks (PR #12) and approved adding the new message types. valueHash, prevHash, transcriptHash, and manifestSha256 stay unverified placeholders until PR #3 is accepted; equality is checked on the values themselves. Signatures stay deferred. The trial does not go through the relay yet.

decision: Term kind codes in count values are lowercase a-z, 0-9, and hyphen, up to 64 characters. code and codes terms must carry a non-empty distinct code list; other types must not. datetime hours are 00-23. An optional term that passes its round limit is dropped and the negotiation continues; a required term ends it. A draft is accepted only when its keys, sheet reference, added term definitions (all fields), and fixed terms equal the rebuild from history. Only approve counts as approval; unknown message types, parties, and decisions are refused. The mock agents refuse to start with a mandate whose ask is outside its own range and escalate instead of sending a value outside it.
reason: The independent verifier of PR #13 showed free text in kind codes and listless code terms, hour 24, optional terms ending the deal, rewritten added definitions and extra draft fields passing, unknown approval decisions counting as approve, and a misconfigured mandate agreeing outside its range.

decision: TermRefuse declines one TermAdd, TermDrop, or TermReopen from the other side: an add request disappears, and a drop or reopen request restores the term's earlier status, value, and proposer. The negotiation continues. Money currencies must be active ISO 4217 codes (iso4217Currencies). Document paths are relative, slash-separated, and refuse a leading slash, backslash, colon, control characters, empty, dot, or dot-dot segments, and segments with surrounding spaces. Non-ASCII file names are allowed.
reason: The director accepted the three recommendations from the PR #13 review: a way to refuse a single request, a real currency list, and path rules that are safe before IX ever handles files.

decision: iso4217Currencies follows the ISO 4217 active list as amended through 2025, including XCG (from 2025-03-31) and VED; it is a fixed list that a person updates. Document paths must already be Unicode NFC and must not contain C0 or C1 controls, bidi controls, zero-width or other invisible fillers, backslash, or colon. Kind codes may not end with a hyphen. Mock mandates with date limits must use real YYYY-MM-DD dates. applyTermMessage checks the whole message shape first and refuses a malformed message instead of throwing. JCS and SHA-256 are merged (PR #3); term digests stay placeholders until the prevHash rule is decided with the reviewer.
reason: The second verification of PR #13 found XCG missing, invisible characters in file names, non-date mandate limits agreeing to any date, and malformed messages throwing. Request and refuse loops are not capped yet; that is decided when the relay carries these messages.

decision: ix:deadline is a deadline value: at (RFC 3339 with offset) and zone (an IANA time zone name or UTC). The offset in at must equal the zone's offset at that instant, including summer time; a date-only deadline is refused. Machines compare only the instant. A duration day is 24 hours counted from the delivery instant, weekends and holidays included; business-day counting would be a separate country-coded term later. Mock deadline mandates name a zone and give ask and limit as RFC 3339 instants; concessions are rendered in the agent's own zone.
reason: The director asked how a date-only deadline handles time of day and countries, and approved deadlines as zoned instants and acceptance windows in calendar days.

decision: A deadline zone must be one of the tzdb 2026e zone.tab names or UTC, spelled exactly (ianaZoneNames, tzdbVersion); aliases such as Asia/Calcutta, US/Pacific, Japan, Etc/UTC, and Etc/GMT offsets are refused, and a person updates the list. A deadline at may not use the -00:00 offset. Document paths also refuse tag characters U+E0000 to U+E007F and the line and paragraph separators U+2028 and U+2029.
reason: The PR #13 verifier found the same zone written several ways (Asia/TOKYO, US/Pacific), -00:00 accepted for UTC, and tag characters and U+2028 passing in file names. The runtime zone list is not used because ICU reports legacy names such as Asia/Calcutta and differs between runtimes. These fixes were written by that verifier at the director's request, so another verifier has to check them.

decision: Nodes must run with Node.js time zone data (process.versions.tz) equal to tzdbVersion in packages/a2a-ext-negotiation/src/zones.ts; verify-ix-node doctor and drive stop otherwise. Offsets and summer-time rules come from that runtime data, so a mismatch would split deadline judgments between nodes. Mock deadline mandates must write ask, latest, and earliest with their own zone's offset, the same check as a deadline value.
reason: The independent verifier of 69b8542 and 85f13e9 showed that the zone list is pinned to tzdb 2026e while offsets come from whatever Node.js ships (Africa/Casablanca changes offset in 2026e), and that a mistyped offset in a mandate limit silently moved the limit by 14 hours. The director chose the runtime version check plus the documented rule.

decision: The director acted as the human security reviewer for PR #3 and merged it. JCS (RFC 8785) and SHA-256 lowercase hex are accepted for canonical bytes and digests. Signatures, keys, JWS, and wiring digests into prevHash still need the security reviewer.
reason: The director checked behavior with concrete examples and a standard sha256sum cross-check, not the code line by line. An engineering security reviewer re-checks before public release.

decision: Contact redaction also removes phones separated by spaces or dots, parenthesized numbers, and HTML-entity at-signs, in every human-facing field and in the agreement. Ordinary prices, dates, and budget numbers stay. docs/retrospective.md records T01 through T15 for the director, including the separate verifier loop.
reason: The verifier's remaining contact shapes were outside the earlier patterns. The retrospective must not copy a personal email address or the previous account handle. PR #3 stays unmerged until a human security reviewer accepts it.

decision: Contact redaction folds Unicode hyphens, the katakana prolonged mark, minus, and middle dots to ASCII separators before matching. It reads (0NN)NNNNNNNN without a separator, at-sign entities without a semicolon, &-encoded entities, @, and the small at sign. Proposal credentials are shown only after redaction. Sentence periods are not folded, so prices and dates next to 。 stay.
reason: An independent verifier showed these shapes and the credentials field still reached the human-facing copy, and that the retrospective credited PR #8 with fixes that only this change makes. Signatures stay deferred. PR #3 stays unmerged.

decision: A phone number is redacted only when it starts with 0 (or a parenthesized area code) and has 10 or 11 digits in total across groups separated by spaces, dots, hyphens, slashes, or tildes, with up to three separator characters between groups. A run preceded by a digit, or by a digit and a separator, is not a phone. ., ., ., %40, and %2e are read as their characters before matching.
reason: A second verifier showed the T16b shapes erased zero-padded dates, postal codes, times, and part numbers from the agreement, and that 03(1234)5678, spaced or slashed separators, and encoded dots still passed. The digit count is the guard against over-redaction. Signatures stay deferred. PR #3 stays unmerged.

decision: A phone may start right after a 1-3 digit prefix and a separator (the prefix is removed with it), and a phone-shaped run is not redacted when a separator and a digit follow immediately, so spaced date and time ranges stay. Known limits: country codes without +, phones after 4+ digit groups or versions, kanji numerals, tab or newline separators. 0-leading 10-11 digit order numbers are redacted as phones.
reason: The third verifier pass on PR #9 found 1-090-1234-5678 kept and 01/05/2026 - 03/31/2026 partly erased. The director chose to close PR #9 with these fixes and a written list of known limits. The current mock draft still carries redacted free text until the agents switch to the typed-term negotiation from PR #13.

decision: A phone-shaped run whose last group has 4 or more digits is redacted even when a separator and a digit follow, so appending -1 or /2026 no longer hides a phone. Runs that end in a 1-3 digit group and continue with a separator and a digit stay, which keeps spaced date and time ranges.
reason: The fourth verifier pass on PR #9 showed that the T16d continuation rule let 090-1234-5678-1 through, including in the agreed deliverables, and that the retrospective wrongly said leaks could not reach the agreement.

decision: PR #9 closes with two more documented limits instead of more patterns: a phone whose last group is cut to 3 or fewer digits before an appended separator and digit stays, and a date or postal code followed by a 4-digit group that together form a phone shape is redacted (as are 0-leading 10-digit ISBNs).
reason: The fifth verifier pass on PR #9 found these and recommended recording them as limits, since pattern redaction cannot be complete and further rules collide with keeping date and time ranges.

decision: Contracts and payments happen outside IX, under each country's law and contract documents, in separate systems. IX hands those systems the agreement and the negotiation transcript as data. What IX must prevent is a false claim about what was said over A2A: fabricated or altered messages, impersonation, a fake human approval, or a transcript with messages removed or reordered. The receiver must be able to check this without trusting an IX node. Signatures in IX are for non-repudiation of the A2A exchange, not a legal e-signature on the contract. Delivery quality, payment, and the truth of entered credentials are out of scope.
reason: The director set this scope. It narrows what the human security reviewer must accept for signatures, JCS, and prevHash, and what the spot lawyer must check. No code changes. Signatures stay deferred. PR #3 (JCS and SHA-256) was merged later the same day (D02).

decision: @ix/agents runTermRelay runs the term-by-term negotiation through the injected relay board. The poster publishes a term job (sheet id, version, sheet sha256 placeholder, preset values, per-term round limit, description) as JobPosting/1 with body record term-job, and both agents publish term messages as x-mock/negotiation-message with body record term. Each side rebuilds its own session only from relay events, decodes each message with decodeTermMessage, refuses events whose issuer does not match the sending party, malformed records, and messages before the job, and shows free text to its human only after contact redaction. No new event kind or tag. Hashes and signatures stay placeholders.
reason: Stage 1 of replacing the legacy free-text negotiation, which the director approved. Drive, nightly, and conformance move in the next stage.

decision: In runTermRelay a job event is used only when its issuer is the poster, its jobId matches the relay tag, and it is the first such event; the poster also requires it to equal the job it posted and stops otherwise. The poster refuses to start with a preset outside its own mandate. decodeTermMessage first takes a strict JSON snapshot that reads each field once and refuses nesting deeper than 64, non-finite numbers, non-plain objects, accessors, symbol keys, __proto__, and unknown fields. Event ids are allocated from the poster and worker ids only, skip taken ids, and ignore suffixes longer than 9 digits.
reason: The independent verifier of PR #15 showed that a third party's fake job made the poster agree to 900,000 JPY against a 180,000 JPY cap, that 3,000-level nesting threw, that one huge event id stopped both sides, and that the decoder rewrote non-JSON values. A fake job that claims the poster's identity is still possible until signatures are checked.

decision: The drive and nightly trial run the term-by-term negotiation: scripts/local-ix.mjs starts the poster and worker as separate processes with createTermSide over the HTTP relay on 127.0.0.1, and scripts/ix-trial-evidence.mjs replays the relay events with @ix/verify verifyTermTranscript (schema, issuers, replay, deadlines) and checks every agreed term against both sample mandates. Sample data is sampleTermJob and the two sample term mandates. The conformance suite still uses the legacy negotiation until stage 2b.
reason: Stage 2a of replacing the free-text negotiation, approved by the director.
